:::{#def-vector-valued-derivative}
#### Derivative of a vector-valued function

If $\vy = \vy(\vb) = \tp{(y_1, \ldots, y_q)}$ is a $q \times 1$ vector-valued function
of the $p \times 1$ vector $\vb$,
its **derivative with respect to** $\vb$
is the $p \times q$ matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is

$$
\sb{\deriv{\vb} \tp{\vy}}_{ij} \eqdef \deriv{\beta_i} y_j,
\qquad i = 1, \ldots, p, \quad j = 1, \ldots, q.
$$

These notes use this *denominator layout* throughout:
rows index the entries of $\vb$ (the denominator)
and columns index the entries of $\vy$ (the numerator),
so column $j$ is the vector derivative $\deriv{\vb} y_j$ (@def-vector-derivative).
Both $\deriv{\vb} \vy$ and $\deriv{\vb} \tp{\vy}$ denote this $p \times q$ matrix.

:::

::: notes
Some sources use the transposed, *numerator layout*,
in which the derivative is the $q \times p$ Jacobian matrix
with $(j, i)$ entry $\deriv{\beta_i} y_j$.
Check a source's layout before combining its formulas with these.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-vector-valued-derivative}
#### Differentiating a $3 \times 1$ function of a $2 \times 1$ vector

Let $\vb = \tp{(\beta_1, \beta_2)}$ ($p = 2$)
and $\vy(\vb) = \tp{(\beta_1^2,\ \beta_1\beta_2,\ 3\beta_2)}$ ($q = 3$).
Then

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vb} \tp{\vy}}_{2 \times 3}
= \sbmat{
\deriv{\beta_1} \beta_1^2 & \deriv{\beta_1} \beta_1\beta_2 & \deriv{\beta_1} 3\beta_2 \\
\deriv{\beta_2} \beta_1^2 & \deriv{\beta_2} \beta_1\beta_2 & \deriv{\beta_2} 3\beta_2
}
= \sbmat{
2\beta_1 & \beta_2 & 0 \\
0 & \beta_1 & 3
}
$$

:::
